summary: preinstall downloads Bun runtime to execute obfuscated bundled payload
details: The package's `preinstall` hook runs `setup.mjs`, which downloads the Bun runtime from GitHub releases, extracts it to a temporary directory, marks it executable, and then invokes the sibling file `math_init.js` under that freshly-fetched runtime via `execFileSync(bunPath, [path.join(D, 'math_init.js')], { stdio:'inherit', cwd: D })`. The executed file is a 727KB single-line script using string-array rotation (a `WV8StW` shuffler), a large mixed hex/character lookup table, a custom decoder, and embedded `with` statements that defeat strict-mode parsers; its filename `math_init.js` has no relationship to the package's declared purpose (ServiceTitan Anvil2 MCP). `setup.mjs` itself is control-flow obfuscated with obfuscator.io-style hex-mangled identifiers (`_0x488df8`, `_0x52943e`) and per-function proxy dictionaries (`YCZJE`, `Hbeql`, `OIvQl`, `MRkzl`). Fetching a second language runtime at install-time solely to execute an obfuscated bundled payload is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern: install-time arbitrary code execution on the installer's host, with the payload delivered via a non-Node runtime to evade scanners that inspect only Node-resolved code, and the lifecycle script obfuscated to hide the flow.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
